reference.readOnlyResponse: This survey is a read-only reference and takes no responses.

results.loadFailed: The results could not be loaded.

fruehwarnsystem.title: Early Warning System
fruehwarnsystem.description: The traffic-light rating of each participant is consolidated into a single picture of the organization. The overall phase is determined by the phase with the highest number of participants, and the volcano displays that phase.
fruehwarnsystem.phasePending: As soon as the first response arrives, the phase of the organization appears here.
fruehwarnsystem.tableCaption: Number and share of participants per phase of the volcano model. The same numbers as in the donut chart.

profiles.title: Profiles
profiles.description: The six resistance profiles referenced by the survey.
profiles.tableCaption: Pattern, description and consequences of the six profiles. This table is always the same and does not depend on the answers.

matrix.title: Mixed Profile Matrix
matrix.description: This matrix shows how a participant's dominant and second-dominant profiles combine to form a new mixed profile. This mixed profile determines the threat, the intervention, the development role, the story and the KPIs.
matrix.tableCaption: Every mixed profile that occurs, sorted by traffic light and frequency. The most dangerous stand at the top.

roadmap.title: Change Risk Roadmap
roadmap.description: For each mixed profile that occurs, two chapters side by side: on the left the risk analysis with threat and intervention, on the right the development path with the new roles and the development story. Red mixed profiles come first.
roadmap.pending: As soon as the first response arrives, the measures appear here.

feedback.title: Impact feedback
feedback.description: Measures whether the survey created trust and whether the measures of the roadmap worked. The total of the three questions falls into one of four impact levels.
feedback.linksHint: The app asks the trust question on the thank-you page right after the survey. The two forms for the end of the journey are shared through these links.
feedback.empty: No feedback yet. As soon as the first answer arrives, the values appear here.
feedback.tableCaption: Mean per question on the scale from 1 to 5. The same numbers as in the bars.
feedback.levelTableCaption: The customer's four impact levels. The total of the three questions decides which one applies.

items.title: Answer overview
items.description: Mean and distribution of every single statement, grouped by profile.
items.tableCaption: Statements of the profile {name} with the mean and the distribution of the answers from 1 to 5.

weighting.title: Profile weighting
weighting.description: Which resistance profiles lead most often in the company and how strong they are on average. Detail for the summary above.
weighting.chartCountsTitle: How often a profile is dominant or second-dominant
weighting.tableCaption: Frequency per profile. The same numbers as in the two charts.

participants.title: Participants
participants.description: The single evaluation is meant above all for managers running surveys with names. It shows the weighted values per profile with the raw block sum below them; expanding a row shows the matching measure.
participants.tableCaption: All participants with the weighted values for the profiles A to F, the dominant and second-dominant profile and the traffic light. The columns can be sorted.

referenceCheck.title: Comparison with the reference evaluation
referenceCheck.description: Every number on this page is checked against the customer's sheets. On the left stands what the app calculates; where something differs, the value from the sheet stands next to it.
referenceCheck.allMatch: Every value matches the CSV files
referenceCheck.participantsCaption: Block sums and weighted values per profile, plus the dominant profile, the second-dominant profile and the traffic light. Every cell shows the app's value; where it differs from the customer's sheet, the sheet value stands below it.
referenceCheck.ampelCaption: The totals from the Frühwarnsystem sheet. The sheet shows two decimals, the app one; the comparison uses one decimal.
referenceCheck.sourcesTitle: Where the comparison values come from
referenceCheck.sourceEvaluation: Internal Survey Responses Evaluation.csv — the block sums
referenceCheck.sourceWeighting: Internal Survey Responses Weighting.csv — the weighted values, the dominant and the second-dominant profile and the traffic light
referenceCheck.sourceFruehwarnsystem: Internal Survey Responses - Frühwarnsystem.csv — the totals per traffic-light value
referenceCheck.contradiction: One place contradicts itself inside the customer's own sheets: the Frühwarnsystem sheet lists participant 8 with F and A, the weighting and roadmap sheets with F and B. F and A would be RED, but that row says YELLOW, and YELLOW is exactly what F and B gives. The comparison therefore follows the weighting sheet.

volcano.explanation: The whole volcano carries the color of the overall phase. The magma chamber says how many participants are in that phase; how high the magma stands in the vent and what comes out of the crater show the same phase. The distribution of all traffic-light values stands beside it on the right.
volcano.srDescription: Cross-section through a volcano. The magma chamber below the ground carries the color of the overall phase: {chamber}. At the crater the drawing shows {crater}. Every number also stands in the table beside it.
volcano.chamberEmpty: still empty, because no responses have arrived yet

crater.ROT: an eruption with a lava fountain, ejected rock and an ash cloud
crater.GELB: a small cloud of smoke above the crater

legend.title: Zone 1 — Magma chamber (invisible layer)
legend.text: Emotions, needs, values, identity, fears, power dynamics. Source of energy and source of risk.

legend.title: Zone 2 — Volcano structure (visible layer)
legend.text: Behaviour, conflicts, processes, communication, roles. Symptoms and forms of expression.

questionnaire.title: Internal Resonance Survey
questionnaire.subtitleAnonymous: Anonymous survey on perceptions of collaboration, change and work culture
questionnaire.subtitleNamed: Survey on perceptions of collaboration, change and work culture

items.A1: I feel that my existing expertise is less valued within the new strategy.
items.A2: It is unclear how my specific expert role will look within the future organizational structure.
items.A3: The new processes/technologies undermine what has made us successful as specialists so far.
items.B1: I would prefer my daily work routines to remain as they currently are and have proven to work.
items.B2: I personally see no meaningful benefit in learning completely new systems at this point.
items.B3: I deliver my solid contribution, but the big strategic leaps should be made by younger/other colleagues.
items.C1: I doubt that the measures planned by top management are sufficient to secure our market position long-term.
items.C2: The new strategy overlooks important logical or operational issues from our real day-to-day work.
items.C3: I consider the defined milestones and strategic goals unrealistic and misaligned with the market.
items.D1: I fear that rapid growth and internationalization will cause us to lose our familiar, family-like culture.
items.D2: The new strategic company values no longer align with my personal values and convictions.
items.D3: I worry that the changes will make us abandon our roots and what defines us as an SME.
items.E1: I am concerned that restructuring will reduce my influence or decision-making power within the team.
items.E2: There is a risk that my previous achievements and informal role in the company will matter less in the future.
items.E3: I feel threatened by the unclear redistribution of tasks and responsibilities.
items.F1: Our daily business is already so dense that I simply have no capacity for additional transformation projects.
items.F2: I feel emotionally exhausted by the speed and amount of simultaneous changes happening in the company.
items.F3: We lack the personnel, financial and time resources needed to implement this new strategy properly.

trust.title: 1.A Participant feedback
trust.description: One question. Goal: psychological safety and trust.

q1.label: Being heard
q1.text: How strongly did the proactive resonance survey give you the feeling that your needs, burdens and concerns during the change were truly heard and taken seriously?

journey.title: 1.B Participant feedback
journey.when: At the end of the journey
journey.description: Three questions: clarity, impact and stability.

q1.label: Clarity
q1.text: How clear was the development path for you (intervention, roles, story)?

q2.label: Impact
q2.text: To what extent did the intervention reduce your burden, conflicts or uncertainties?

q3.label: Stability
q3.text: How stable do you feel in your new role (e.g. Resilience Champion, Relationship Builder)?

leader.title: 2. Leader feedback
leader.when: At the end of the journey
leader.description: Three questions for the people responsible: visible change, reduced risk and team impact.

q1.label: Visible change?
q1.text: How clearly is the positive change in behavior or collaboration observable?

q2.label: Risk reduced?
q2.text: To what extent has the original risk (e.g. overload, status conflicts) decreased?

q3.label: Team impact
q3.text: To what extent has the participant's development improved team stability?

low.name: Low impact
low.interpretation: The intervention has barely taken effect. The risk remains.

moderate.name: Moderate impact
moderate.interpretation: Partial improvement, but unstable. The risk is only slightly reduced.

high.name: High impact
high.interpretation: The intervention is clearly effective. Behavior and stability visibly improve.

veryHigh.name: Very high impact
veryHigh.interpretation: The intervention is fully effective. The risk is practically neutralized.

A.name: Identity Expert
A.beschreibung: Identity rests on knowledge that is under threat. (Fear of losing significance)
A.folgen: Massive factual criticism as a shield, hoarding of knowledge.
A.impactRationale: 130 %: highest impact. It threatens the self-image of the German expert culture. Ignored, it turns into hidden, highly intelligent sabotage.

B.name: Preservation-Oriented Employee
B.beschreibung: Inner resignation, a wish for quiet.
B.folgen: Working strictly to rule, disinterest, „We have always done it this way“.
B.impactRationale: 80 %: lower impact. It leads to passive withdrawal rather than active destruction.

C.name: Strategic Skeptic
C.beschreibung: Does not believe that the new strategy works in technical terms.
C.folgen: Direct criticism in low-context cultures; „technical detail questions“ in high-context cultures.
C.impactRationale: 90 %: dampening. Pure factual criticism, valuable data, emotionally manageable.

D.name: Culture Keeper
D.beschreibung: Fear of losing values and identity.
D.folgen: Pointing back to „the good old days“, worry about the fabric of the team.
D.impactRationale: 100 %: neutral. Important on the values level; good sense-making stabilises it.

E.name: Status-Anxious Employee
E.beschreibung: Fear of losing power, influence or security.
E.impactRationale: 120 %: very high impact. It triggers informal power struggles that block whole teams.

F.name: The Overloaded
F.beschreibung: Wants the strategy but has no capacity.
F.folgen: High sick leave, signs of burnout, „We will never manage that“.
F.impactRationale: 85 %: lower impact. A pure resource problem; stopping a project or more budget solves it quickly.

A+B.bedrohung: Inner Resignation: Loss of creativity, mechanical execution of tasks
A+B.ziel: Competence Building & Self-Efficacy: Revitalizing innovation power

A+C.bedrohung: Creeping Standstill: Strategy is logically dismantled, workforce gets pulled into skepticism
A+C.ziel: Strategic Precision: Using expertise for improvement instead of blockage

A+D.bedrohung: Cultural Rebellion: Blocking new initiatives out of moral obligation
A+D.ziel: Preserve Cultural Identity: Translating core values into the new organizational future

A+E.bedrohung: Destructive Explosion: Highly intelligent sabotage, open power struggles, project breakdown
A+E.ziel: Clarity of Power & Stability: Resolving hidden power struggles, restoring leadership effectiveness

A+F.bedrohung: Systemic Collapse: Loss of key personnel (burnout, resignation)
A+F.ziel: Resilience & Capacity Building: Relief as a prerequisite for change readiness

B+C.bedrohung: Productive Tension: Creativity meets logic; no escalation

B+D.bedrohung: Thick Lava Flow: Sarcasm, cynicism, working strictly to rule
B+D.ziel: Stability & Psychological Safety: Defining routines, reducing pressure

B+E.bedrohung: Showcase Tension: Creativity distorted by status pressure; frustration & withdrawal
B+E.intervention: Creative Impact Alignment; Role Clarification; Protected Spaces for Creativity
B+E.ziel: Balance between Creativity & Recognition; genuine effectiveness

B+F.bedrohung: Creativity Erosion: Exhaustion slows ideas; frustration & withdrawal
B+F.intervention: Resource Rebalancing; Stop-Doing; Protected Creativity Phases

C+D.bedrohung: Delays from Logic-Culture Conflict: Subtle tensions, mistrust, devaluation
C+D.intervention: Sense-Making & Decision Alignment; Role Clarification; Shared Decision Principles; Team Norms Workshop
C+D.ziel: Integration of Logic & Culture; respectful decision processes; clear principles; cohesive team identity

C+E.bedrohung: Paralyzing Process Gridlock: Political pseudo-debates block decisions
C+E.ziel: Strengthening Decision-Making: Separating logic from politics

C+F.bedrohung: Delays: Deadlines slip, but no sabotage
C+F.ziel: Realistic Planning: Time buffers & resources for sustainable implementation

D+E.bedrohung: Status Collides with Culture: Hidden loyalty conflicts, misunderstandings, declining cohesion
D+E.intervention: Values Alignment; Role Clarification; Team Norms Workshop; Feedback Rituals; Moderated Dialogue
D+E.ziel: Balance between Recognition & Culture; psychological safety; cohesive team

D+F.bedrohung: Loyalty Overload: Sense of duty collides with exhaustion; guilt & overwhelm
D+F.intervention: Team Care; Role Clarification; Healthy Team Norms

E+F.bedrohung: Burnout Escalation: Performance pressure meets overload; breakdown, withdrawal, errors, conflicts
E+F.intervention: Capacity Reset; Resource Rebalancing; Stop-Doing; Expectation Alignment; Psychological Safety
E+F.ziel: Sustainable Performance; clear priorities; balance between expectations & capacity; stable resilience
E+F.kpis: Resilience ↑, clarity of priorities ↑, error rate ↓

A>E.name: The Significance-Anxious
A>E.story: After clarification, the participant develops the strength of a Mentor who provides orientation, and simultaneously the capability of a Relationship Builder who gains influence through cooperation rather than status.

E>A.name: The Status-Insecure Expert
E>A.story: The participant learns to use relationships instead of power and gains stability. At the same time, they unfold the qualities of a Mentor who gives the team safety and direction.

A>F.name: The Overloaded Identity Holder
A>F.story: The participant grows into the role of a Mentor who shares responsibility and simultaneously develops the resilience of a Champion who enables healthy performance.

F>A.name: The Overloaded Identity Holder
F>A.story: The participant strengthens their resilience and learns to set clear priorities. At the same time, they develop the qualities of a Mentor who stabilizes the team.

A>D.name: The Values-Blocking Expert
A>D.story: The participant combines the strength of a Mentor with the role of a Values Ambassador. They translate culture into the new organizational world and give the team orientation.

D>A.name: The Duty-Driven Preserver
D>A.story: The participant develops into a Values Ambassador who creates meaning, and simultaneously into a Mentor who supports change with stability.

E>F.name: The Pressure-Overloaded Performer
E>F.story: The participant gains clarity in relationships and strengthens their resilience. They become a stable, cooperative force within the team.

F>E.name: The Overloaded Status Seeker
F>E.story: The participant reduces overload and develops resilience. At the same time, they strengthen their ability to shape relationships constructively.

B>D.name: The Duty-Routine Preserver
B>D.story: The participant develops the ability to create stable structures while also conveying values. They become a reliable, culturally grounded force in the team.

D>B.name: The Values-Routine Carrier
D>B.story: The participant combines value awareness with structural clarity. They create both meaning and order, strengthening team cohesion.

A>C.name: The Logic-Dismantling Expert
A>C.story: The participant uses their experience as a Mentor and combines it with the analytical strength of a Quality Navigator. Critique becomes quality, experience becomes orientation.

C>A.name: The Strategic-Dismantling Analyst
C>A.story: The participant develops precise quality orientation and simultaneously the ability to support others as a Mentor. The dynamic becomes constructive and strategically clear.

A>B.name: The Routine-Frozen Expert
A>B.story: The participant combines inspiring orientation with stable structure. They create safety and meaning, strengthening the team’s ability to change.

B>A.name: The Stability-Focused Specialist
B>A.story: The participant develops clear routines and simultaneously the ability to provide direction as a Mentor. The team gains focus and motivation.

C>E.name: The Political-Analytical Blocker
C>E.story: The participant separates logic from politics and simultaneously strengthens their relational capability. Decisions become clearer and more trustworthy.

E>C.name: The Status Politician
E>C.story: The participant strengthens relationships and simultaneously develops analytical clarity. Collaboration becomes efficient and cooperative.

E>D.name: The Loyalty-Conflict Carrier
E>D.story: The participant gains recognition through relationships rather than status and combines this with cultural clarity. The team becomes more cohesive.

D>E.name: The Recognition-Seeking Preserver
D>E.story: The participant brings values into the team and simultaneously strengthens relationships. The dynamic becomes trusting and stable.

D>C.name: The Culture-Logic Conflict Carrier
D>C.story: The participant combines cultural stability with logical precision. Decisions become respectful and clear.

C>D.name: The Logic-Culture Analyst
C>D.story: The participant structures complex topics while simultaneously conveying values. Change becomes both rational and culturally supported.

B>E.name: The Creativity-Blocked Recognition Seeker
B>E.story: The participant creates safe frameworks and simultaneously strengthens relationships. Creativity becomes possible again.

E>B.name: The Recognition-Focused Routine Carrier
E>B.story: The participant brings closeness and simultaneously develops structure. The team gains balance and focus.

B>F.name: The Exhausted Routine Carrier
B>F.story: The participant creates order and simultaneously develops resilience. The team becomes stable and robust.

F>B.name: The Overloaded Stability Seeker
F>B.story: The participant strengthens their resilience and simultaneously develops structural competence. The dynamic becomes sustainable.

D>F.name: The Duty-Overloaded Preserver
D>F.story: The participant combines value awareness with resilience. The team gains emotional and physical stability.

F>D.name: The Overloaded Loyalty Carrier
F>D.story: The participant develops healthy performance capability and simultaneously cultural clarity. Change becomes sustainable.

B>C.name: The Structured Innovator
B>C.story: The participant combines stable structure with precise quality. The productive tension strengthens innovation and efficiency.

C>B.name: The Precise Stability Thinker
C>B.story: The participant develops clear priorities and simultaneously stable routines. The team works focused and safely.

F>C.name: The Realistic Planner
F>C.story: The participant strengthens their resilience and simultaneously develops analytical clarity. Deadlines become realistic and achievable.

C>F.name: The Analytical Resilience Navigator
C>F.story: The participant structures tasks and simultaneously develops healthy performance capability. Collaboration becomes sustainable and efficient.
